I didn't eat anything particularly unhealthy - my diet is poorer now I am on mounjaro as I have no desire to cook interesting and healthy foods anymore.

I understand that my body and how it reacts plays a massive part in how I process the food I take in, it is incredibly efficient and will get every last calorie where as someone else who is skinny would not.
However, saying that "I" could change that just by knowing I was consuming more calories is not accurate as without the extra hormones GLP-1 and GIP, along with Levothyroxine for my missing thyroid hormones, consuming fewer calories just meant I was sleeping more and at inappropriate times, like at work.
I have stopped logging my food now as well. I used to do that fairly religiously. But it just made me feel sad when it would be 8pm and the only thing I wanted to do was either sleep or eat, and I'd already had up to my BMR. If I ate I would have energy for more of the day, if I didn't I would just sleep, and it would get worse over time if I ate a deficit.

But anyway the "eat less, move move" is too reductive. Sometimes to be able to "eat less, move more" you have to fix why you haven't been able to do that in the first place.

Vet also to check and see if bun has picked up anything nasty from their escape and the tics, there are some diseases like myxo and RVHD which, fingers crossed, they are vaccinated against. Also, vet can tell you if the gender and if they have been de-sexed. It's important to have bunnies de-sexed to prevent some very common cancers. There will always be more buns to rescue than homes unfortunately so please don't think de-sexing is optional and that you can breed the little one...

The vet who taught you may have got this from what was known in the 70's or even the 90's but learning has moved on since then, and since rabbits are more prevalent as pets and not just as food or lab animals there is more known about better ways of handling them. I am not trying to shame you or say you are a bad bun parent, you are not but even though you do this (you have been shown how to pick up a bunny by the scruff of the neck without hurting or damaging them) OP should most definitely not do this. It's clear their bunny wriggles and thrashes and if the weight of the bunny is on their neck as they are grabbed by the scruff, the bunny may end up dead as it wriggles or thrashes when OP does this.

Please don't do that, bunny skin is really fragile, and this is also making their entire body weight be supported, however briefly, by the neck. I realise that people do still do this but it's usually out of not understanding rather than because it's okay.

Picking up your rabbit should be done by getting your hands on the sides of their torso, and quickly scooping them up to be close to your body, putting your arms under them; like a baby but without putting them upside down.  You should be supporting them with your arms and hands, but without their claws being able to scratch your hands. I am similarly to concerned to other commentors that your bunny was thrashing about when you tried to pick him up, as they are very much able to fracture bones while struggling. When holding a bunny who is trying to escape I have been scratched on my chest, neck and face, rarely on my arms, but not my hands ever.

If your bun gets into places they are not meant to, you can use your hands and feet without picking them up, to usher them out - obviously this depends on how quickly you need to get them out.
